summary: This section sets out the rules for determining the compensatory award in unfair dismissal claims, establishing that tribunals must award an amount that is just and equitable based on the financial loss attributable to the employer's actions. It incorporates expenses and lost benefits into the calculation while requiring the claimant to observe the common law duty to mitigate loss. The section also directs deductions or reductions for contributory fault, protected disclosures made without good faith, and certain redundancy payments.

elements.requirement: The compensatory award must reflect what is just and equitable based on loss caused by the dismissal that is attributable to the employer's conduct.
elements.quote: such amount as the tribunal considers just and equitable in all the circumstances having regard to the loss sustained by the complainant in consequence of the dismissal in so far as that loss is attributable to action taken by the employer

elements.requirement: Compensable loss includes reasonably incurred expenses resulting from the dismissal.
elements.quote: any expenses reasonably incurred by the complainant in consequence of the dismissal

elements.requirement: Compensable loss includes benefits the complainant would reasonably have expected to receive had they not been dismissed.
elements.quote: loss of any benefit which he might reasonably be expected to have had but for the dismissal

elements.requirement: Loss of redundancy payments or expectations thereof is limited to the extent they exceed the basic award.
elements.quote: only the loss referable to the amount (if any) by which the amount of that payment would have exceeded the amount of a basic award

elements.requirement: The tribunal must apply common law rules regarding the claimant's duty to mitigate their loss.
elements.quote: the tribunal shall apply the same rule concerning the duty of a person to mitigate his loss as applies to damages recoverable under the common law

elements.requirement: Industrial action or threats of industrial action pressured upon the employer must be disregarded when determining the employer's responsibility for the loss.
elements.quote: no account shall be taken of any pressure which by— (a) calling, organising, procuring or financing a strike or other industrial action, or (b) threatening to do so, was exercised on the employer to dismiss the employee

elements.requirement: The tribunal must reduce the compensatory award by a just and equitable proportion if the complainant's conduct caused or contributed to the dismissal.
elements.quote: Where the tribunal finds that the dismissal was to any extent caused or contributed to by any action of the complainant, it shall reduce the amount of the compensatory award by such proportion as it considers just and equitable having regard to that finding

elements.requirement: The tribunal may reduce the award if the dismissal was for a protected disclosure that was not made in good faith.
elements.quote: Where— (a) the reason (or principal reason) for the dismissal is that the complainant made a protected disclosure, and (b) it appears to the tribunal that the disclosure was not made in good faith, the tribunal may, if it considers it just and equitable in all the circumstances to do so, reduce any award it makes to the complainant by no more than 25%

elements.requirement: Any employer redundancy payment in excess of the payable basic award must be deducted from the compensatory award.
elements.quote: If the amount of any payment made by the employer to the employee on the ground that the dismissal was by reason of redundancy (whether in pursuance of Part XI or otherwise) exceeds the amount of the basic award which would be payable but for section 122(4), that excess goes to reduce the amount of the compensatory award

elements.requirement: An award made under section 112(5) must be deducted when calculating the compensatory award for the purposes of section 117(3)(a).
elements.quote: there shall be deducted from the compensatory award any award made under section 112(5) at the time of the order under section 113

thresholds.what: Maximum permitted reduction to an award where a protected disclosure was not made in good faith
